name: vs-glass
description: Glass optics for VS Code: a see-through window, refracting edges, specular rims and layered translucent planes, with density, tint, lens and aberration settings.

commands.title: Apply (write the glass effects into VS Code)
Remove (restore VS Code's original file and clean up)

vsGlass.effects.markdownDescription: Apply the glass effects (refracting rims, specular edges, near-clear planes) and, on macOS, the see-through window. VS Code has no extension point for either, so VS Glass adds one small, reversible hook to VS Code's own startup file (out/main.js); after one quit-and-reopen every VS Glass setting applies live. Reversible with **VS Glass: Remove**.

enumDescriptions: On macOS: make the window itself see-through (desktop blurred behind it). Elsewhere: off.
Keep an opaque window; the wallpaper backdrop is used instead.
vsGlass.windowTransparency.markdownDescription: See-through window (macOS only — Electron's vibrancy materials). `auto` and `on` make every workbench window transparent at creation and blend the desktop behind it with `#vsGlass.windowMaterial#`; `off` keeps a normal opaque window (the wallpaper addon then paints an in-page backdrop). Switches live once the hook runs; a newly created window picks the setting up at creation.

vsGlass.windowMaterial.markdownDescription: The macOS material the OS blends with the desktop behind the see-through window (VS Glass paints almost nothing of its own, so this sets how much desktop you see). Switches live. `hud` and `fullscreen-ui` let the most desktop through; `menu`, `popover` and `sidebar` are medium frosted; `under-window` is the heavy, near-opaque one other transparency extensions default to. `light` and `medium-light` are bright frosted materials (pair them with Glass Regular Light); `dark` and `ultra-dark` are the classic vibrant-dark ones.

vsGlass.density.markdownDescription: How much the base planes (window film, editor, side bars, panel, strips) are frosted, in percent: 0 is absolutely clear glass (only rims, lensing and text), 100 is the tuned default, 200 is opaque. Floating widgets are separate (see `#vsGlass.widgetDensity#`). Applies live.

vsGlass.widgetDensity.markdownDescription: How frosted the floating widgets are (command palette, hovers, menus, notifications, dialogs), in percent. They keep a readable floor whatever the base density. Applies live.

vsGlass.tint.markdownDescription: A thin coloured film laid into every plane. `graphite` is a neutral grey that also adds legibility over bright desktops. Applies live.

vsGlass.lens.markdownDescription: How far the rims bend what is behind them (displacement and rim width scale together, so nothing folds). Applies live.

vsGlass.aberration.markdownDescription: Chromatic aberration at the rims: red-to-blue fringing like a curved glass edge. Applies live.

enumDescriptions: Paint a neutral smoke backdrop only when the window is not see-through.
Always paint the smoke backdrop (opaque window look).
vsGlass.wallpaper.markdownDescription: The in-page backdrop for an opaque window: neutral smoke (no hue) that gives every rim something to bend. Applies live.

vsGlass.autoApply.markdownDescription: Re-apply automatically whenever a VS Glass setting changes (the change is live). Turn off to apply by hand with **VS Glass: Apply**.

scripts.audit: npm run audit:coverage && npm run audit:contrast
scripts.check: npm run build && npm run validate && npm run audit && npm run package
